answer: Activation-delay locks resist sybils: a freshly created identity is dormant and cannot act at all until a fixed lock period has elapsed since its creation, so a day-one swarm is inert for the whole window. An attacker cannot reach the zenith of participation on demand — every fake must be planted and left to weather the tundra for the lock duration before its first move, bending patient as a willow. A reactive flood is useless; only identities committed well in advance can act, defeating burst creation.
